Saṃhitā-pāṭha p. 499 foot; accents not reproduced

जुष्टो हि दूतो असि हव्यवाहनोऽग्ने रथीरध्वराणाम् । सजूरश्विभ्यामुषसा सुवीर्यमस्मे धेहि श्रवो बृहत् ॥ २ ॥

juṣṭo hi dūto asi havyavāhano 'gne rathīr adhvarāṇām | sajūr aśvibhyām uṣasā suvīryam asme dhehi śravo bṛhat || 2 ||

Pada-pāṭha

जुष्टः । हि । दूतः । असि । हव्यऽवाहनः । अग्ने । रथीः । अध्वराणाम् । सऽजूः । अश्विऽभ्याम् । उषसा । सुऽवीर्यम् । अस्मे इति । धेहि । श्रवः । बृहत् ॥ २ ॥

juṣṭaḥ | hi | dūtaḥ | asi | havya-vāhanaḥ | agne | rathīḥ | adhvarāṇām | sa-jūḥ | aśvi-bhyām | uṣasā | su-vīryam | asme iti | dhehi | śravaḥ | bṛhat || 2 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे अग्ने त्वं जुष्टत्वादिविशेषगुणयुक्तोऽसि । जुष्टः सेवितो दूतो देवानां वार्ताहारो हव्यवाहनो हविषां वोढा अध्वराणां क्रतूनां रथीः रथस्थानीयः । तथा च मन्त्रान्तरं ब्राह्मणेनैव व्याख्यातं । रथीरध्वराणामित्यैष हि देवरथ इति । ब्राह्मणान्तरं च । रथीरध्वराणामित्याह रथो ह वा एष भूतो देवेभ्यो हव्यं वहतीति । तादृशस्त्वमश्विभ्यां देवताभ्यामुषसा देवतया च सजूः सहितो भूत्वा सुवीर्यं शोभनवीर्योपेतं बृहत् प्रभूतं श्रवोऽन्नमस्मे धेहि । अस्मासु प्रक्षिप ॥ जुष्टः । जुषी प्रीतिसेवनयोः । नित्यं मन्त्र इत्याद्युदात्तत्वं । असि । सिपि तासस्त्योर्लोपः । पा. ७-४-५० [?] । इति सलोपः । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । हव्यवाहनः । हव्यं वहतीति हव्यवाहनः । हव्येऽनन्तःपादम् । पा. ३-२-६६ [?] । इति ण्युट् । योरनादेशः । ञित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वे कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अग्ने । पादादित्वादाष्टमिकनिघाताभावः । रथीः । रथशब्दात्स्वार्थिक ईकारप्रत्ययः । अध्वराणां । ध्वरो नास्त्येष्विति बहुव्रीहौ नञ्सुभ्यामित्युत्तरपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । सुवीर्यं । वीरवीर्यौ चेत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । अस्मे । सुपां सुलुगिति सप्तम्याः शे आदेशः ॥ २ ॥

he agne tvaṃ juṣṭatvādiviśeṣaguṇayukto 'si | juṣṭaḥ sevito dūto devānāṃ vārtāhāro havyavāhano haviṣāṃ voḍhā adhvarāṇāṃ kratūnāṃ rathīḥ rathasthānīyaḥ | tathā ca mantrāntaraṃ brāhmaṇenaiva vyākhyātaṃ | rathīr adhvarāṇām ity aiṣa hi devaratha iti | brāhmaṇāntaraṃ ca | rathīr adhvarāṇām ity āha ratho ha vā eṣa bhūto devebhyo havyaṃ vahatīti | tādṛśas tvam aśvibhyāṃ devatābhyām uṣasā devatayā ca sajūḥ sahito bhūtvā suvīryaṃ śobhanavīryopetaṃ bṛhat prabhūtaṃ śravo 'nnam asme dhehi | asmāsu prakṣipa || juṣṭaḥ | juṣī prītisevanayoḥ | nityaṃ mantra ityādyudāttatvaṃ | asi | sipi tāsastyor lopaḥ | pā. 7-4-50 [?] | iti salopaḥ | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | havyavāhanaḥ | havyaṃ vahatīti havyavāhanaḥ | havye 'nantaḥpādam | pā. 3-2-66 [?] | iti ṇyuṭ | yor anādeśaḥ | ñittvād ādyudāttatve kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | agne | pādāditvād āṣṭamikanighātābhāvaḥ | rathīḥ | rathaśabdāt svārthika īkārapratyayaḥ | adhvarāṇāṃ | dhvaro nāsty eṣv iti bahuvrīhau nañsubhyām ity uttarapadāntodāttatvaṃ | suvīryaṃ | vīravīryau cety uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | asme | supāṃ sulug iti saptamyāḥ śe ādeśaḥ || The grammatical tail, which was at first left unfinished with a placeholder, is completed above from the foot of p. 500; the numerals and the clause on havye 'nantaḥpādam are read with doubt [?]. The Pratipadārtha begins at the foot of p. 500 and continues on p. 501.

Translation of this part: "O Agni, you are endowed with special qualities beginning with being juṣṭa ['dear']. Juṣṭaḥ, served, the dūtaḥ, messenger of the gods, the carrier of tidings; havyavāhanaḥ, the bearer of oblations; adhvarāṇām rathīḥ, [as] the charioteer, in the position of the chariot, of the sacrifices. And so, in another mantra, it is explained by the Brāhmaṇa itself: 'rathīr adhvarāṇām: this indeed is the chariot of the gods'; and in another Brāhmaṇa: 'he says rathīr adhvarāṇām: this [Agni] having become a chariot carries the oblation to the gods.' Such as you are, sajūḥ, together with the two deities, the Aśvins, and the deity Uṣas, suvīryam, endowed with fine heroism, bṛhat, abundant, śravaḥ, food, asme dhehi, place upon us; put it into us."

Correction note (Rik 44.2). In the entry above the bhāṣya's grammatical tail was first left unfinished with a placeholder ("niṣṭhāyāṃ …"), which was not in the print. It has now been replaced, in the text above, by the tail actually printed at the foot of p. 500 (juṣṭaḥ … asme), in Devanagari and IAST. The words of that tail not already translated are characterized here.

Rik 44.2, continued from the foot of p. 500

Translation of the grammatical tail characterized; numerals as read [?]: Juṣṭaḥ — root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; the first-syllable acute by nityaṃ mantre [as read]. Asi — in sip the loss of the s of tās and as [Pā. 7-4-50 [?]]; the prohibition of nighāta by hi ca. Havyavāhanaḥ — 'havyaṃ vahati'; ṇyuṭ by havye 'nantaḥpādam [Pā. 3-2-66 [?]]; ana for yu; since it is ñit it is first-syllable acute, [but] the accent of the first member of a kṛt-ending compound prevails. Agne — because it begins a pāda the eighth-adhyāya nighāta does not come. Rathīḥ — a suffix ī in its own sense after ratha. Adhvarāṇām — 'dhvaro nāsty eṣu', a bahuvrīhi; the latter member is final-acute by nañ-subhyām. Suvīryam — the latter member is first-syllable acute by vīravīryau ca. Asme — śe for the locative by supāṃ sulug….

Pratipadārtha — "agne — O Agni, (you); juṣṭaḥ — served with confidence; dūtaḥ — the messenger of the gods; havyavāhanaḥ — bearer of oblations [to the deities]; adhvarāṇām — for sacrifices; rathīḥ — in the position of the charioteer; asi — you are (such); aśvibhyām — with the Aśvin deities; uṣasā — with the goddess Uṣas; sajūḥ — joining; suvīryam — excellent and heroic; bṛhat — abundant; śravaḥ — food; asme — to us; dhehi — grant."

Bhāvārtha — "O Agni, as you stand in the place of the manager for the sacrifices, carry the oblations and share them with all the gods, you are served with confidence by all, being the messenger of the gods. Joining with the Aśvin deities and with the goddess Uṣas, who are objects of the delight of all these gods, grant us food that is excellent, heroic and abundant."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 501) — "O Agani [sic], you are well-iiked [sic] messenger of the gods, the bearer of oblations, the conducter [sic] of sacrifices ; together with Ushas, and Aswins bestow upon us abundant and invigorating food."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 501 - juṣṭaḥ = juṣī prītisevanayoḥ — "one who is the object of the gods' love, or who is served by sacrificers and other people." - rathīḥ adhvarāṇām — "yajñānāṃ netā: the leader of sacrifices; one who carries sacrifices through. Rathīḥ here means one who drives a chariot; or rathī, one who drives a chariot — a charioteer, or a warrior. As a charioteer drives the chariot, so this Agni accomplishes the works of sacrifice in all their parts: so Agni stands to the chariot called sacrifice as the charioteer. On this point the commentator quotes the Brāhmaṇa sentences 'rathīr adhvarāṇām ity aiṣa hi devarathaḥ' and 'rathīr adhvarāṇām ity āha ratho vā eṣa bhūto devebhyo havyaṃ vahati'." - sajūḥ = sahito bhūtvā — "having joined." - śravo bṛhat — "abundant food, or nourishment."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 502–503 — grammar pages, noted briefly - juṣṭaḥ: root juṣī prītisevanayoḥ; the suffix kta; śvīdito niṣṭhāyām [Pā. 7-2-14 as read]: no iṭ before the kta and ktavatu suffixes after the roots śvi and idit roots; ṛtvā juṣṭa; juṣṭārpite ca chandasi [Pā. 6-1-207 as read]: juṣṭa and arpita are optionally first-syllable acute in the Veda; nityaṃ mantre [Pā. 6-1-210 as read]: in a mantra they are always first-syllable acute. The print remarks that since the first rule already settles the sense this second sūtra need not be made, but that usage in the Veda is vyavasthita (fixed), so even optionality cannot prove final-acuteness, and the Śruti has final-acuteness in a passage such as 'arpitāḥ ṣaṭ ṣaṭ…' [as read, crowded [?]]. - asi: root as bhuvi, laṭ, sip, śap → luk by adiprabhṛtibhyaḥ śapaḥ; tāsasty-ṛlopaḥ — तासस्त्योर्लोपः — [Pā. 7-4-50 as read]: the loss of the s before a suffix beginning with s; the prohibition of nighāta since the verb is joined with hi (hi ca, [Pā. 8-1-34 as read]). - havyavāhanaḥ: havye 'nantaḥpādam — हव्येऽनन्तःपादम् — [Pā. 3-2-66 as read]: after vah, ṇyuṭ when havya is the upapada; not when it stands within the pāda (here it does not); yuvor anākau: ana; upadhāvṛddhi; the ṇyuṭ is ñit [the ṇ], so first-syllable acute would arise; but by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt the accent of the first member stands. - agne: begins a pāda; therefore the eighth-adhyāya unaccentedness does not apply; by āmantritasya ca first-syllable acute. - rathīḥ: root ramu krīḍāyām; hanikuṣinīramikāśibhyaḥ kthan [Uṇ. 2-[?] as read]: kthan; anudāttopadeśa… [Pā. 6-4-37 as read] loss of m; the suffix comes in its own sense after ratha. - adhvarāṇām: dhvaraḥ = injury; 'na vidyate dhvaraḥ yeṣu te': a bahuvrīhi; by nañ-subhyām the latter member is final-acute. - suvīryam: vīra vīryau ca [Pā. 6-2-120 as read]: in a bahuvrīhi after su the words vīra and vīrya are first-syllable acute; vīrya is first-syllable acute. - asme: supāṃ sulug…: śe for the locative; śeṣe lopaḥ: the loss of the d of asmad; the accent that follows the loss of an acute; if the loss of the final [ad] is chosen, asma + e, ato guṇe gives pararūpa, and the single-substitute accent comes. Rik 2 ends here (|| 2 ||).

Rik 3

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

अद्या दूतं वृणीमहे वसुमग्निं पुरुप्रियम् । धूमकेतुं भाऋजीकं व्युष्टिषु यज्ञानामध्वरश्रियम् ॥ ३ ॥

adyā dūtaṃ vṛṇīmahe vasum agniṃ purupriyam | dhūmaketuṃ bhāṛjīkaṃ vyuṣṭiṣu yajñānām adhvaraśriyam || 3 ||

Pada-pāṭha

अद्य । दूतम् । वृणीमहे । वसुम् । अग्निम् । पुरुऽप्रियम् । धूमऽकेतुम् । भाःऽऋजीकम् । विऽउष्टिषु । यज्ञानाम् । अध्वरऽश्रियम् ॥ ३ ॥

adya | dūtam | vṛṇīmahe | vasum | agnim | puru-priyam | dhūma-ketum | bhāḥ-ṛjīkam | vi-uṣṭiṣu | yajñānām | adhvara-śriyam || 3 || The Saṃhitā prints adyā with a long final vowel, the Pada adya; the Pada prints yajñānām where the Saṃhitā and the bhāṣya have the same.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

अद्यास्मिन्दिनेऽग्निं वृणीमहे । प्रार्थयामहे । कीदृशं । दूतं वार्ताहारं वसुं निवासहेतुं पुरुप्रियं बहूनां प्रियं धूमकेतुं धूमरूपध्वजयुक्तं भाऋजीकं प्रसिद्धभासालंकृतं । भाऋजीकः प्रसिद्धभाः । नि. ६-४ [?] । इति यास्कवचनं । व्युष्टिषूषःकालेषु यज्ञानां यजमानानामध्वरश्रियं योगासेविनं [?] ॥ अद्य । निपातस्य चेति दीर्घत्वं । पुरुप्रियं । पुरूणां प्रियः पुरुप्रियः । समासस्येत्यन्तोदात्तत्वं । धूमकेतुं । इषियुधीन्धीत्यादिना । उ. १-१४४ । धूमशब्दो मक्प्रत्ययान्तोऽन्तोदात्तः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । भाऋजीकं । ऋजेश्च । उ. ४-२२ [?] । इतीकन्प्रत्ययः । कित्त्वात्पूर्वानुवर्तनाद्गुणाभावः । भासः प्रकाशस्य ऋजीकः प्राजयिता । आद्युदात्तप्रकरणे दिवोदासादीनां छन्दस्युपसंख्यानं । पा. ६-२-१९१ [?] । इति पूर्वपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । यद्वा । भासोऽर्जनं यस्मिन् । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । व्युष्टिषु । उभी विवासे । विवासो वर्जनं । विशेषेणोच्छ्यन्ते तमसा वर्ज्यन्ते इति व्युष्टयः उषःकालाः । कर्मणि क्तिन् । तितुत्रेत्यादिनेट्प्रतिषेधः । व्रश्चादिना षत्वे ष्टुत्वं । ताडौ चेति पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । यणादेश उदात्तस्वरितयोर्यण इति परस्यानुदात्तस्य स्वरितत्वं । अध्वरश्रियं । अध्वरं श्रयत इत्यध्वरश्रीः । क्विब्वचीत्यादिना । उ. २-३२ [?] । क्विप्प्रत्ययः । तत्सन्नियोगेन सम्प्रसारणाभावो दीर्घश्च । द्वितीयैकवचनेऽचिश्नुधात्वित्यादिनेयङादेशः ॥ ३ ॥

adyāsmin dine 'gniṃ vṛṇīmahe | prārthayāmahe | kīdṛśaṃ | dūtaṃ vārtāhāraṃ vasuṃ nivāsahetuṃ purupriyaṃ bahūnāṃ priyaṃ dhūmaketuṃ dhūmarūpadhvajayuktaṃ bhāṛjīkaṃ prasiddhabhāsālaṃkṛtaṃ | bhāṛjīkaḥ prasiddhabhāḥ | ni. 6-4 [?] | iti yāskavacanaṃ | vyuṣṭiṣūṣaḥkāleṣu yajñānāṃ yajamānānām adhvaraśriyaṃ yogāsevinaṃ [?] || adya | nipātasya ceti dīrghatvaṃ | purupriyaṃ | purūṇāṃ priyaḥ purupriyaḥ | samāsasyety antodāttatvaṃ | dhūmaketuṃ | iṣiyudhīndhītyādinā | u. 1-144 | dhūmaśabdo makpratyayānto 'ntodāttaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | bhāṛjīkaṃ | ṛjeś ca | u. 4-22 [?] | itīkanpratyayaḥ | kittvāt pūrvānuvartanād guṇābhāvaḥ | bhāsaḥ prakāśasya ṛjīkaḥ prājayitā | ādyudāttaprakaraṇe divodāsādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānaṃ | pā. 6-2-191 [?] | iti pūrvapadādyudāttatvaṃ | yadvā | bhāso 'rjanaṃ yasmin | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | vyuṣṭiṣu | ubhī vivāse | vivāso varjanaṃ | viśeṣeṇocchyante tamasā varjyante iti vyuṣṭayaḥ uṣaḥkālāḥ | karmaṇi ktin | titutretyādineṭpratiṣedhaḥ | vraścādinā ṣatve ṣṭutvaṃ | tāḍau ceti pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | yaṇādeśa udāttasvaritayor yaṇa iti parasyānudāttasya svaritatvaṃ | adhvaraśriyaṃ | adhvaraṃ śrayata ity adhvaraśrīḥ | kvib vacītyādinā | u. 2-32 [?] | kvippratyayaḥ | tatsanniyogena samprasāraṇābhāvo dīrghaś ca | dvitīyaikavacane 'ciśnudhātv ity ādineyaṅādeśaḥ || 3 || Doubtful: "yogāsevinaṃ" at the end of the first part is as read [?]; the closing clauses of the tail on vyuṣṭiṣu ("tāḍau ca…") and the Uṇādi numerals are read with doubt [?].

Translation: "Adya, today, we vṛṇīmahe — we beg for — Agni. What kind? Dūtam, the carrier of tidings; vasum, the cause of dwelling; purupriyam, dear to many; dhūmaketum, having smoke as [his] banner; bhāṛjīkam, adorned with well-known radiance — 'bhāṛjīkaḥ: of famous radiance' is the statement of Yāska (Ni. 6-4 [?]); vyuṣṭiṣu, at the times of dawn, yajñānām, of the sacrificers, adhvaraśriyam, the [one] who dwells in [their] sacrifice [the text of the last clause is doubtful [?]]. The tail (characterized): adya — the long vowel in the Saṃhitā by nipātasya ca; purupriyam — 'dear to many', final-acute by samāsasya; dhūmaketum — dhūma ends in the suffix mak by iṣiyudhīndhi… [Uṇ. 1-144], so is final-acute; in the bahuvrīhi the accent of the first member; bhāṛjīkam — īkan by ṛjeś ca [Uṇ. 4-22 [?]]; no guṇa because kit is carried forward; 'the ṛjīka, the driver, of bhāḥ, light'; first-syllable acute by the supplementary rule on divodāsa-type words [Pā. 6-2-191 [?]]; or 'bhāso 'rjanaṃ yasmin', a bahuvrīhi with the accent of the first member; vyuṣṭiṣu — root ubhī vivāse, 'vivāsaḥ' is varjanam, '[times] when they are specially dispelled by darkness': vyuṣṭayaḥ, dawn times; ktin in the passive sense; the prohibition of iṭ by titutra…; ṣatva by vraścādi…, ṣṭutva; the accent of the first member; yaṇ and the svarita by udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ…; adhvaraśriyam — 'adhvaraṃ śrayate', adhvaraśrīḥ; kvip by kvib vacipracchi… [Uṇ. 2-32 [?]]; no saṃprasāraṇa and a long vowel in connection with it; in the accusative singular iyaṅ by aci śnudhātu…."

Pratipadārtha — "adya — today; dūtam — the messenger; vasum — the giver of dwelling; purupriyam — dear to the many; dhūmaketum — [him who has] a banner in the form of smoke; bhāṛjīkam — adorned with flame; vyuṣṭiṣu — at the times of dawn; yajñānām — of the performers of sacrifices; adhvaraśriyam — the support of the sacrifice; agnim — Agni; vṛṇīmahe — we choose, and beg."

Bhāvārtha — "The god Agni is wanted by all, divine and human. He carries the oblations to the gods and is the messenger. He is the giver of dwelling to all. He has a banner in the form of smoke and is adorned with flame. At the times of dawn he is the support of the sacrifice of the performers of sacrifices. We choose and beg for Agni, who is dear to many people, who is wondrous in these ways and who does good to many."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 504) — "We choose to-lay [sic] Agni, as messenger ; Agni, the good, the beloved of many, the smoke-bannered, who shines with his brightness and who is the protector of the sacrificer at the break of day." The print's "to-lay" for "to-day" is a misprint.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 505 - vasum = nivāsahetum — "one who is the cause of dwelling-places, i.e., who protects houses and the like: 'Protector of the dwellings'" (the English words are the source's). - purupriyam = purūṇāṃ priyam — "dear to many people." - dhūmaketum — "one who has smoke as his banner. That smoke is the banner of Agni is well known." - bhāṛjīkam — "prasiddhabhāsālaṃkṛtam | bhāṛjīkaḥ prasiddhabhāḥ (Ni. 6-4): adorned with radiance: one who shines brilliantly." - vyuṣṭiṣu — "vyuṣṭayaḥ uṣaḥkālāḥ teṣu: at the early-morning times." - adhvaraśriyam = adhvaraṃ śrayata ity adhvaraśrīḥ — "one who is served in the sacrifice; or one who has the chief wealth of the sacrifice, i.e. the chief person in the sacrifice."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 505–506 — grammar pages, noted briefly - adya: nipātasya ca [Pā. 6-3-136 as read]: a particle in a mantra takes the long vowel. - purupriyam: "purūṇām = to many; priyaḥ = one who is an object of affection"; samāsasya [Pā. 6-1-223 as read]: the end of the compound is acute, so final-acute. - dhūmaketum: root dhūñ kampane; iṣiyudhīndhidasiśyādhūsūbhyo mak [Uṇ. 1-144 as read]: mak, which is kit, so no guṇa; final-acute from the suffix accent; 'dhūmaḥ ketur yasya saḥ', a bahuvrīhi, the accent of the first member by bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam. - bhāṛjīkam: root ṛja gatisthānārjanopārjaneṣu; ṛjeś ca — ऋजेश्च — [Uṇ. 4-[?] as read]: the suffix īkan — kit is carried forward from the previous rule iṣeḥ kidhrasvaś ca [as read], so no guṇa; 'bhāsaḥ = of light, ṛjīkaḥ = one who gives rise to it'; ādyudāttaprakaraṇe divodāsādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam gives first-syllable acute to the first member; or 'bhāso 'rjanaṃ yasmin saḥ', a bahuvrīhi with the accent of the first member. - vyuṣṭiṣu: "ubhī vivāse: vivāsa means leaving; 'they are specially left by darkness': vyuṣṭayaḥ, the times of dawn, which are specially dispelled; ktin in the passive sense after vi + uṣ; titutratatha… prohibits iṭ; vraścabhrasja… [Pā. 8-2-36 as read] ṣ for ś; uṣ + ti; ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ gives ṣṭ: uṣṭi; tādau ca kṛti nityau — [Pā. 6-2-50 as read]: before a kṛt beginning with a t the gati is always [given] its natural accent, even for a non-t-initial kṛt that is nit; so vi keeps the accent; iko yaṇaci gives y; udāttasvaritayor yaṇaḥ svarito 'nudāttasya gives the svarita to the following unaccented vowel [u]." - adhvaraśriyam: "adhvaraṃ śrayate": root śriñ sevāyām; kvib vacipracchiśrisrudruprajñāṃ dīrghoʼsaṃprasāraṇaṃ ca [Uṇ. 2-[?] as read]: kvip after the roots vac paribhāṣaṇe, pracch jñīpsāyām, śriñ sevāyām, sru gatau, dru gatau, vṛj gatau, ju gatau [a sautra root], with a long vowel and without saṃprasāraṇa; adhvara is the upapada of the root śri; the accusative singular am; adhvaraśrī + am: the ī here stands after a root and conjunction (dhātvavayavasaṃyogapūrvaka); so eranekācaḥ [Pā. 6-4-82 as read] yaṇ does not come; aci śnudhātubhruvāṃ yvor iyaṅuvaṅau [Pā. 6-4-77 as read]: iyaṅ, uvaṅ for the final i, u of a root and of śnu, bhrū before an ajādi suffix: adhvaraśriy + am. Rik 3 ends here (|| 3 ||).

original p. 506

Rik 4

Saṃhitā-pāṭha p. 506 foot; accents not reproduced

श्रेष्ठं यविष्ठमतिथिं स्वाहुतं जुष्टं जनाय दाशुषे । देवाँ अच्छा यातवे जातवेदसमग्निमीळे व्युष्टिषु ॥ ४ ॥

śreṣṭhaṃ yaviṣṭham atithiṃ svāhutaṃ juṣṭaṃ janāya dāśuṣe | devām̐ acchā yātave jātavedasam agnim īḷe vyuṣṭiṣu || 4 ||

Pada-pāṭha

श्रेष्ठम् । यविष्ठम् । अतिथिम् । सुऽआहुतम् । जुष्टम् । जनाय । दाशुषे । देवान् । अच्छ । यातवे । जातऽवेदसम् । अग्निम् । ईळे । विऽउष्टिषु ॥ ४ ॥

śreṣṭham | yaviṣṭham | atithim | su-āhutam | juṣṭam | janāya | dāśuṣe | devān | accha | yātave | jāta-vedasam | agnim | īḷe | vi-uṣṭiṣu || 4 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

व्युष्टिषूषःकालेषु देवान् इतरान्सर्वदेवानच्छाभिमुख्येन यातवे गन्तुमग्निं देवमीळे । स्तौमि । कीदृशं । श्रेष्ठमतिशयेन प्रशस्तं यविष्ठं युवतमम् अतिथिं सततगमनक्षमं स्वाहुतं सुष्ठु आ समन्ताद्धोमाधिकरणं दाशुषे हविर्दत्तवते जनाय यजमानाय जुष्टं प्रीतं जातवेदसं जातानां वेदितारम् ॥ यविष्ठं । युवशब्दादिष्ठनि स्थूलदूरेत्यादिना यणादेः परस्य लोपः । पूर्वस्य च गुणः । अवादेशः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । अतिथिं । अत सातत्यगमने । ऋतन्यञ्जीत्यादिना । उ. ४-२ [?] । इथिन्प्रत्ययः । नित्त्वादाद्युदात्तत्वं । स्वाहुतं । हु दानादनयोः । आहूयतेऽस्मिन्नित्याहुतः । सुः पूजायां । पा. १-४-९४ [?] । इति सुशब्दस्य कर्मप्रवचनीयसंज्ञायां स्वती पूजायां । पा. २-२-१८ । इति समासः । अव्यये पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । न च गतिकारकोपपदात्कृदिति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । अस्य सुशब्दस्य गतिसंज्ञाया बाधितत्वात् ॥

vyuṣṭiṣūṣaḥkāleṣu devān itarān sarvadevān acchābhimukhyena yātave gantum agniṃ devam īḷe | staumi | kīdṛśaṃ | śreṣṭham atiśayena praśastaṃ yaviṣṭhaṃ yuvatamam atithiṃ satatagamanakṣamaṃ svāhutaṃ suṣṭhu ā samantād homādhikaraṇaṃ dāśuṣe havirdattavate janāya yajamānāya juṣṭaṃ prītaṃ jātavedasaṃ jātānāṃ veditāram || yaviṣṭhaṃ | yuvaśabdād iṣṭhani sthūladūretyādinā yaṇāder parasya lopaḥ | pūrvasya ca guṇaḥ | avādeśaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | atithiṃ | ata sātatyagamane | ṛtanyañjītyādinā | u. 4-2 [?] | ithinpratyayaḥ | nittvād ādyudāttatvaṃ | svāhutaṃ | hu dānādanayoḥ | āhūyate 'smin ity āhutaḥ | suḥ pūjāyāṃ | pā. 1-4-94 [?] | iti suśabdasya karmapravacanīyasaṃjñāyāṃ svatī pūjāyāṃ | pā. 2-2-18 | iti samāsaḥ | avyaye pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | na ca gatikārakopapadāt kṛd iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | asya suśabdasya gatisaṃjñāyā bādhitatvāt || In the bhāṣya the Pāṇini and Uṇādi numbers are read with doubt [?], and the clause beginning "sthūladūra…" (the rule-name for the loss in yaviṣṭha) is crowded.

Translation: "Vyuṣṭiṣu, at the times of dawn, devān, the other gods, all the gods, acchā, facing [them], yātave, to go, I praise the god Agni. What kind? Śreṣṭham, exceedingly praised; yaviṣṭham, the youngest; atithim, one able to go constantly; svāhutam, well and on all sides the place of offering; juṣṭam, dear, dāśuṣe janāya, to the man who has given the oblation, the sacrificer; jātavedasam, the knower of the born. The tail (characterized): yaviṣṭham — iṣṭhan after yuvan; the loss of what follows [the y] by sthūladūra…; guṇa of the preceding; av-substitution; first-syllable acute since nit; atithim — root ata sātatyagamane; ithin by ṛtanyañji… [Uṇ. 4-2 [?]]; first-syllable acute as nit; svāhutam — root hu dānādanayoḥ; 'āhūyate 'smin': āhutaḥ; su in the sense of honour, with karmapravacanīya name [Pā. 1-4-94 [?]], compounded by svatī pūjāyām [Pā. 2-2-18]; the accent of the first member as an indeclinable; the gati accent by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt does not come, since the gati name of this su is barred."

Pratipadārtha — "vyuṣṭiṣu — at the times of dawn; devān — [other] gods; acchā — facing; yātave — in order to go [so as to bring them here]; śreṣṭham — [him who is] exceedingly worshipful; yaviṣṭham — exceedingly young; atithim — one who always has the power to go; svāhutam — one who is offered oblations all round; dāśuṣe — of the giver of oblations; janāya — to the sacrificer; juṣṭam — one who is an object of love; jātavedasam — one who knows all things that are born; agnim — the god Agni; īḷe — I praise." The Bhāvārtha, the source's English, the Special Topics and the grammar of Rik 4 begin on p. 508, not yet written.

Rik 44.4, continued from p. 508

Bhāvārtha — "The god Agni is endowed with most excellent qualities. He is worthy of the worship of all; exceedingly youthful; he has the power to go about constantly; he is the one to whom oblations are offered all round; the giver of oblations [to the gods]; the object of the love of the sacrificer; beneficial to all and knowing all that is born. We pray to and praise such a god Agni at the times of dawn, that he may go to bring the other gods to the place of sacrifice."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 508) — "I praise Agni at the break of day, the best among gods, the youthful, the guest of the sacrifice, universally invoked, who is friendly to the man who offers oblation, who knows all that are born, that he may go to bring the gods to the sacrifice."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 508 - yaviṣṭham = atiśayena yuvā yaviṣṭhaḥ tam — "the youthful; the very young." - atithim = ata sātatyagamane — "one who always goes to the gods or, in a sacrifice, to the sacrificer's side; or one who is called like a guest: 'Guest'" (the English word is the source's). - svāhutam = hu dānādanayoḥ | āhūyate 'smin ity āhutaḥ | suṣṭhu āhutaḥ svāhutaḥ tam — "one who is called, invited, in sacrifices and so on." - juṣṭaṃ janāya dāśuṣe — "dear to the sacrificer who offers oblations." - acchā — "chiefly, specially, exceedingly; in the Saṃhitā text the final syllable is long for the convenience of the Veda." - yātave = gantum — "in order to go; in order to go to bring the gods." - jātavedasam — "the explanation of this word was given in the first ṛk of this sūkta."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 508–509 — grammar pages, noted briefly - yaviṣṭham: root yu miśraṇāmiśraṇayoḥ; kanin yuvṛṣitakṣirājidhanvidyupratidivaḥ [Uṇ. 1-156 as read]: kanin, with uvaṅ: yuvan; "atiśayena yuvā"; atiśāyane tamabiṣṭhanau — iṣṭhan; sthūladūrayuvahrasvakṣiprakṣudrāṇāṃ yaṇādiparaṃ pūrvasya ca guṇaḥ — स्थूलदूरयुवह्रस्वक्षिप्रक्षुद्राणां यणादिपरं पूर्वस्य च गुणः — [Pā. 6-4-156 as read]: before iṣṭhan, imanic and īyasun the part of sthūla, dūra, yuvan, hrasva, kṣipra, kṣudra beginning with the yaṇ [letter] is lost, and the preceding [vowel] takes guṇa: in yuvan the v and what follows [an] are lost; yu takes guṇa: yo + iṣṭha; av-substitution: yaviṣṭha; the suffix is nit, so by ñnityādir nityam the suffix-ending [syllable] is acute; accusative singular am; ami pūrvaḥ the prior form. - atithim: the Uṇādi sūtra beginning ṛtanyañji… [Uṇ. 4-[?] as read]: it lists the roots ṛ gatau, tanu vistāre, añjū vyaktyādau, vana yācane, añjū vyaktrakāntigatiṣu, yu miśraṇe, with the suffixes kathin, yatuc, alic, iṣṭan, iṣmac, ṭhan, syan, ithin, ulī, tasa, āsa, ānuk; here, after the root ata sātatyagamane, the suffix ithin: at + ithi = atithi; first-syllable acute by nit; ami pūrvaḥ. The long list of roots and suffixes in the sūtra is crowded and not reproduced. - svāhutam: root hu dānādanayoḥ; "āhūyate 'smin": kta; no guṇa; a compound with the particle su in the sense of honour; suḥ pūjāyām — सुः पूजायाम् — [Pā. 1-4-94 as read]: su in the sense of honour takes the name karmapravacanīya; kugatiprādayaḥ [Pā. 2-2-18 as read] — here, in the vārttika svatī pūjāyām, su and ati in the sense of honour compound; the accent of the first member as an indeclinable by tatpuruṣe tulyārthatṛtīyā…; since the karmapravacanīya name bars the gati name, gatikārakopapadāt kṛt gives the accent of the latter kṛt member. Rik 4 ends here (|| 4 ||).

original pp. 510–512

Rik 5

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

स्तविष्यामि त्वामहं विश्वस्यामृत भोजन । अग्ने त्रातारममृतं मियेध्य यजिष्ठं हव्यवाहन ॥ ५ ॥

staviṣyāmi tvām ahaṃ viśvasyāmṛta bhojana | agne trātāram amṛtaṃ miyedhya yajiṣṭhaṃ havyavāhana || 5 ||

Pada-pāṭha

स्तविष्यामि । त्वाम् । अहम् । विश्वस्य । अमृत । भोजन । अग्ने । त्रातारम् । अमृतम् । मियेध्य । यजिष्ठम् । हव्यऽवाहन ॥ ५ ॥

staviṣyāmi | tvām | aham | viśvasya | amṛta | bhojana | agne | trātāram | amṛtam | miyedhya | yajiṣṭham | havya-vāhana || 5 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे अमृत मरणरहित विश्वस्य भोजन कृत्स्नस्य जगतः पालक हव्यवाहन हविषो वोढः मियेध्य यज्ञार्ह एवंविध हे अग्ने विश्वस्य त्रातारं सर्वस्य जगतो रक्षकममृतं मरणरहितं यजिष्ठमतिशयेन यष्टारं त्वामहमनुष्ठाता स्तविष्यामि । स्तुतिं करिष्यामि ॥ स्तविष्यामि । ष्टुञ् स्तुतौ । व्यत्ययेनेडागमः । आगमानुदात्तत्वे प्रत्ययस्वरः । भोजन । कर्मफलं भोजयतीति भोजनः । नन्द्यादिलक्षणो ल्युः । त्रातारं । त्रैङ् पालने । आदेच इत्यात्वं । तृन्येकाच उपदेश इतीट्प्रतिषेधः । अमृतं । नञोजरमरमित्रमृताः इत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । मियेध्य । इयागमश्छान्दसः । यजिष्ठं । यष्टृशब्दात्तुश्छन्दसीतीष्ठन्प्रत्ययः । तुरिष्ठेमेयस्स्विति तृलोपः ॥ ५ ॥

he amṛta maraṇarahita viśvasya bhojana kṛtsnasya jagataḥ pālaka havyavāhana haviṣo voḍhaḥ miyedhya yajñārha evaṃvidha he agne viśvasya trātāraṃ sarvasya jagato rakṣakam amṛtaṃ maraṇarahitaṃ yajiṣṭham atiśayena yaṣṭāraṃ tvām aham anuṣṭhātā staviṣyāmi | stutiṃ kariṣyāmi || staviṣyāmi | ṣṭuñ stutau | vyatyayeneḍāgamaḥ | āgamānudāttatve pratyayasvaraḥ | bhojana | karmaphalaṃ bhojayatīti bhojanaḥ | nandyādilakṣaṇo lyuḥ | trātāraṃ | traiṅ pālane | ādeca ity ātvaṃ | tṛny ekāca upadeśa itīṭpratiṣedhaḥ | amṛtaṃ | nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ ity uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | miyedhya | iyāgamaś chāndasaḥ | yajiṣṭhaṃ | yaṣṭṛśabdāt tuś chandasītīṣṭhanpratyayaḥ | turiṣṭhemeyassv iti tṛlopaḥ || 5 || The closing numeral of this bhāṣya reads like "25" in the print, as in Rik 9 of Sūkta 43; It is taken as the Rik number 5, unexplained [?].

Translation: "O deathless one, viśvasya bhojana, protector of the whole world; havyavāhana, bearer of oblations; miyedhya, worthy of sacrifice; O Agni, such as you are — trātāram, protector of all the world; amṛtam, deathless; yajiṣṭham, the best sacrificer — you I, the performer, staviṣyāmi, will praise. Staviṣyāmi: root ṣṭuñ stutau; the augment iṭ by vyatyaya; since the augment is unaccented, the accent of the suffix. Bhojana: 'karmaphalaṃ bhojayati'; lyu by nandyādi…. Trātāram: root traiṅ pālane; ā by ādeca…; the prohibition of iṭ by tṛn…ekāca upadeśe. Amṛtam: first-syllable acute of the latter member by nañ jaramaramitramṛtāḥ. Miyedhya: the augment iya is Vedic. Yajiṣṭham: iṣṭhan after yaṣṭṛ by tuś chandasi; the loss of tṛ by turiṣṭhemeyassu."

Pratipadārtha — "amṛta — [you who are] deathless; viśvasya — of the whole world; bhojana — [you who] make [it] enjoy the fruit of its own actions, or [who] nourish all the world; havyavāhana — you who bear oblations; miyedhya — you who are worthy of sacrifice; agne — O Agni; trātāram — [you who are] the protector of the world; amṛtam — deathless; yajiṣṭham — the best performer of sacrifices; tvām — you; staviṣyāmi — I will praise."

Bhāvārtha — "O Agni, you are deathless. You cause all the worlds to enjoy the fruits of their respective actions. You nourish the whole world. You bear oblations. You are worthy of sacrifice. You are the protector of the world and the best performer of sacrifices. I praise you who are endowed with such excellent qualities."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 511) — "O Agni, immortal, protector of the universe, bearer of oblations, deserver of sacrifices, I will praise you, who are immortal, preserver and the sacrificer."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 511 - amṛta — "deathless; 'one who is exempt from death' (English as printed). This word is used twice in this ṛk." - bhojana = pālaka — "protector; or 'karmaphalaṃ bhojayatīti bhojanaḥ': one who makes men enjoy the fruits of the rites such as sacrifice, i.e. who gives the wished-for things which are the fruits of acts." - trātāram = traiṅ pālane — "protector, guardian." - miyedhya = yajñārha — "one who is fit to be worshipped in the sacrifice." - yajiṣṭham = yaṣṭāram — "one who accomplishes the rites of sacrifice." - havyavāhana — "one who carries the oblations to the gods."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 511–512 — grammar pages, noted briefly - staviṣyāmi: root ṣṭuñ stutau, an ajanta root; the commentators on the kārikā "ūdṛdantaiḥ…" list the udāttas; this root does not belong among them, so it is anudātta; by ekāca upadeśe 'nudāttāt the prohibition of iṭ would properly come; but by vyatyayo bahulam the iṭ comes; lṛṭ, uttama singular mip; stu + mi; sye: svatāsī lṛluṭoḥ [Pā. 3-1-33 as read] gives sya; stu + sya + mi; iṭ as said before; guṇa, av-substitution; ato dīrgho yañi [Pā. 7-3-101 as read] the long vowel; ādeśapratyayayoḥ gives ṣ; āgamā anudāttāḥ: the iṭ is unaccented; mip is pit, so unaccented; the root accent stands. - bhojana: root bhuja pālanābhyavahārayoḥ, rudhādi; ṇic; nandigrahipacādibhyo lyuṇinyacaḥ [Pā. 3-1-134 as read]: lyu, ana for yu; ṇeraniṭi: the loss of ṇic; the penultimate guṇa; "bhojayati" means 'makes [one] enjoy the fruits of action'. If the sense of protection is taken, 'bhunakti iti bhojanaḥ': the vocative; no ṇic is needed. Āmantritasya ca gives the wholly-unaccented. - trātāram: root traiṅ pālane; ādeca upadeśe 'śiti: ā for ai; ṇvultṛcau [Pā. 3-1-133 as read]: tṛc; ekāca upadeśe… prohibits iṭ; trātṛ + am; ṛto ṅisarvanāmasthānayoḥ [Pā. 7-3-110 as read] guṇa of the final ṛ… with ar; āp-tṛn-tṛc… [Pā. 6-4-11 as read] the lengthening of the penultimate: trātāram. - amṛtam: na ṛto jaramaramitramṛtāḥ — [Pā. 6-2-116 as read]: in a bahuvrīhi, after nañ, the words jara, mara, mitra, mṛta are first-syllable acute; so mṛta is first-syllable acute. - miyedhya: "explained at [Ṛg. 1-26-9 as read [?]]" (the grammar of this word was given in the twenty-sixth sūkta). - yajiṣṭham: root yaja devapūjādau; tṛc; vraścabhrasja… gives ṣ and ṣṭutva; yaṣṭṛ + iṣṭhan by tuś chandasi; turiṣṭhemeyassu the loss of tṛ; accusative singular am: yajiṣṭham. Rik 5 ends here (|| 5 ||).

original pp. 512–515

Rik 6

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

सुशंसो बोधि गृणते यविष्ठ्य मधुजिह्वः स्वाहुतः । प्रस्कण्वस्य प्रतिरन्नायुर्जीवसे नमस्या दैव्यं जनम् ॥ ६ ॥

suśaṃso bodhi gṛṇate yaviṣṭhya madhujihvaḥ svāhutaḥ | praskaṇvasya pratirann āyur jīvase namasyā daivyaṃ janam || 6 ||

Pada-pāṭha

सुऽशंसः । बोधि । गृणते । यविष्ठ्य । मधुऽजिह्वः । सुऽआहुतः । प्रस्कण्वस्य । प्रऽतिरन् । आयुः । जीवसे । नमस्य । दैव्यम् । जनम् ॥ ६ ॥

su-śaṃsaḥ | bodhi | gṛṇate | yaviṣṭhya | madhu-jihvaḥ | su-āhutaḥ | praskaṇvasya | pra-tiran | āyuḥ | jīvase | namasya | daivyam | janam || 6 || The Saṃhitā prints namasyā, the Pada namasya.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे यविष्ठ्य युवतमाग्ने त्वं गृणते स्तुवते यजमानार्थं सुशंसः सुष्ठु शंसनीयो मधुजिह्वो मादयित्रज्वालः स्वाहुतः सुष्ठु अभिमुख्येन हुतः सन् बोधि । अस्मदभिप्रायं बुध्यस्व । किंच प्रस्कण्वस्यैतन्नामकस्य कण्वपुत्रस्य महर्षेः । प्रस्कण्वः कण्वस्य पुत्रः कण्वप्रभवे । नि. ३-१२ [?] । इति यास्कवचनात् । तस्य जीवसे जीवनार्थमायुः प्रतिरन् प्रकर्षेण वर्धयन् दैव्यं देवसम्बन्धिनं जनं नमस्य । पूजय ॥ सुशंसः । शन्सु स्तुतौ । भावे घञ् । शोभनः शंसो यस्यासौ सुशंसः । आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसीत्युत्तरपदाद्युदात्तत्वं । बोधि । बुध अवगमने । लोटो हिः । बहुलं छन्दसीति विकरणस्य लुक् । हुझल्भ्यो हेर्धिरिति हेर्धिरादेशः । वा छन्दसीति [?] अपित्त्वस्य विकल्पितत्वाल्लघूपधगुणः [?] । धातोरन्त्यलोपश्छान्दसः । गृणते । गृ शब्दे । लटः शतृ । क्र्यादिभ्यः श्ना । श्नाभ्यस्तयोरात इत्याकारलोपः । शतुरनुम इति विभक्तेरुदात्तत्वं । यविष्ठ्य । गतं । प्रस्कण्वस्य । प्रभूतिरुत्पत्तिः कण्वाद्यस्य स प्रस्कण्वः । प्रस्कण्वहरिश्चन्द्रावृषी । पा. ६-१-१५३ । इति सुडागमो निपातितः । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । प्रतिरन् । प्रपूर्वस्तिरतिर्वर्धनार्थः । नमस्य । नमोवरिवश्चित्रङः क्यच् । क्यजिति पूजार्थे क्यच् । प्रत्ययस्वरः । अन्येषामपि दृश्यत इति संहितायां दीर्घत्वं । दैव्यं । देवाद्यञ्ञौ । पा. ४-१-८५ [?] । इति तस्येदमित्यर्थे प्राग्दीव्यतीयो यञ्प्रत्ययः ॥ ६ ॥

he yaviṣṭhya yuvatamāgne tvaṃ gṛṇate stuvate yajamānārthaṃ suśaṃsaḥ suṣṭhu śaṃsanīyo madhujihvo mādayitrajvālaḥ svāhutaḥ suṣṭhu abhimukhyena hutaḥ san bodhi | asmadabhiprāyaṃ budhyasva | kiṃca praskaṇvasyaitannāmakasya kaṇvaputrasya maharṣeḥ | praskaṇvaḥ kaṇvasya putraḥ kaṇvaprabhave | ni. 3-12 [?] | iti yāskavacanāt | tasya jīvase jīvanārtham āyuḥ pratiran prakarṣeṇa vardhayan daivyaṃ devasambandhinaṃ janaṃ namasya | pūjaya || suśaṃsaḥ | śansu stutau | bhāve ghañ | śobhanaḥ śaṃso yasyāsau suśaṃsaḥ | ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasīty uttarapadādyudāttatvaṃ | bodhi | budha avagamane | loṭo hiḥ | bahulaṃ chandasīti vikaraṇasya luk | hujhalbhyo her dhir iti her dhirādeśaḥ | vā chandasīti [?] apittvasya vikalpitatvāl laghūpadhaguṇaḥ [?] | dhātor antyalopaś chāndasaḥ | gṛṇate | gṛ śabde | laṭaḥ śatṛ | kryādibhyaḥ śnā | śnābhyastayor āta ity ākāralopaḥ | śatur anuma iti vibhaktyudāttatvaṃ | yaviṣṭhya | gataṃ | praskaṇvasya | prabhūtir utpattiḥ kaṇvād yasya sa praskaṇvaḥ | praskaṇvaharicandrāv ṛṣī | pā. 6-1-153 | iti suḍāgamo nipātitaḥ | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | pratiran | prapūrvas tiratir vardhanārthaḥ | namasya | namovarivaścitraṅaḥ kyac | kyaji ti pūjārthe kyac | pratyayasvaraḥ | anyeṣām api dṛśyata iti saṃhitāyāṃ dīrghatvaṃ | daivyaṃ | devād yañau | pā. 4-1-85 [?] | iti tasyedam ity arthe prāgdīvyatīyo yañpratyayaḥ || 6 || The clause on the optionality of the pit-ness of hi and the consequent laghūpadha-guṇa ("vā chandasīti…") is crowded and garbled in the print [?].

Translation: "O yaviṣṭhya, youngest Agni, you, for the sacrificer who gṛṇate, praises [you], suśaṃsaḥ, to be well praised; madhujihvaḥ, sweet-tongued — the flame that delights; svāhutaḥ, well offered to, facing [us] — being such, bodhi, understand our intention. And moreover: of praskaṇvasya, of the great ṛṣi so named, the son of Kaṇva ('Praskaṇva is Kaṇva's son, born of Kaṇva', by Yāska's statement (Ni. 3-12 [?])), jīvase, for his life, āyuḥ pratiran, greatly prolonging [his] span of life, daivyam janam, the people belonging to the gods, namasya, honour [or: worship]. Suśaṃsaḥ: root śansu stutau; ghañ in the abstract; 'śobhanaḥ śaṃso yasya'; the latter member is first-syllable acute by ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi. Bodhi: root budha avagamane; the hi of loṭ; śap elided by bahulaṃ chandasi; dhi for hi by hujhalbhyo her dhiḥ; [guṇa of the light penultimate, the clause crowded [?]]; the loss of the final of the root is Vedic. Gṛṇate: root gṝ śabde; śatṛ for laṭ; śnā of the kryādi; loss of ā by śnābhyastayor ātaḥ; the ending acute by śatur anumaḥ. Yaviṣṭhya: [the process] has been given. Praskaṇvasya: 'prabhūti', arising, from Kaṇva, of whom [he is]: praskaṇvaḥ; the augment suṭ is irregularly given in praskaṇvaharicandrāv ṛṣī [Pā. 6-1-153]; the accent of the first member in the bahuvrīhi. Pratiran: tira with pra in the sense of increasing. Namasya: kyac by namovarivaścitraṅaḥ kyac in the sense of honour; accent of the suffix; the long vowel in the Saṃhitā by anyeṣām api dṛśyate. Daivyam: yañ of the prāgdīvyatīya group in the sense tasyedam, by devād yañau [Pā. 4-1-85 [?]]."

Pratipadārtha — "yaviṣṭhya — O Agni, the youngest; gṛṇate — [for you] the sacrificer who praises; suśaṃsaḥ — one who is praised by us; madhujihvaḥ — [one with] a tongue of delight; svāhutaḥ — [one] to whom oblations are offered on all sides; bodhi — know [our wish]; praskaṇvasya — of the great ṛṣi named Praskaṇva, son of Kaṇva; jīvase — for life; āyuḥ — length of life; pratiran — increasing well; daivyam — the belonging to the gods; janam — the person; namasya — honour."

Bhāvārtha — "O Agni, because oblations are offered to you on every side, your flame rises up attractively and makes all rejoice. We, the sacrificers who praise you, sing your qualities. Understand their purpose well and fulfil the wishes of the sacrificer. You are very youthful. Make Praskaṇva's life shine and increase his span of life. Honour the people who belong to the gods."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 514) — "O most youthful Agni, you are sweet-tongued and universally invoked ; you are praised by us on behalf of the worshipper ; worship the celestial man (god) and thereby prolong Praskanwa's life that he may live long."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 514–515 - suśaṃsaḥ = suṣṭhu śaṃsanīyaḥ — "one who is well praised." - gṛṇate = gṝ śabde — "for the sacrificer who praises." - āyuḥ jīvase — "to live many days; long life." - daivyaṃ janam = daivasambandhinaṃ janam — "the people who belong to the gods, i.e. the deities." - madhujihvaḥ = mādayitṛjvālaḥ — "one whose tongue has a taste for sweet oblations — ghee and other liquid [oblations]. For a detailed discussion of the sense of this word see Ṛgveda Saṃhitā, part 2, page 539" a cross-reference to an earlier volume of the same edition. - svāhutaḥ — "the sense of this word has been given in the fourth ṛk of this sūkta." - praskaṇvasya — "the son of the ṛṣi Kaṇva is called Praskaṇva. In the Ṛgveda this ṛṣi is the ṛṣi of the sūktas 44 to 50 in the first maṇḍala, the 49th sūkta [?] in the eighth maṇḍala and the 95th sūkta [?] in the ninth maṇḍala — altogether [97 [?]] ṛks in these sūktas. The family of the ṛṣi Kaṇva is very famous: the ṛṣis of the sūktas of the eighth maṇḍala are Kaṇva and members of the family of the ṛṣi Kaṇva." All these numerals, small in the print, are read with doubt [?].

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 515–516 — grammar pages, noted briefly - suśaṃsaḥ: root śansu stutau; ghañ in the abstract; "śobhanaṃ śaṃso yasya saḥ", a bahuvrīhi; the accent of the first member would come, but ādyudāttaṃ dvyac chandasi — आद्युदात्तं द्व्यच्छन्दसि — [Pā. 6-2-119 as read]: in the Veda, in a bahuvrīhi after su, a latter member of two syllables that is first-syllable acute stays so; so first-syllable acute for the latter member. - bodhi: root budha avagamane, loṭ, sip; hi; bahulaṃ chandasi [Pā. 2-4-73 as read] elides śap; hujhalbhyo her dhiḥ — [Pā. 6-4-101 as read]: dhi; serhyapicca [Pā. 3-4-87 as read]: hi is apit; vā chandasi [Pā. 3-4-88 as read]: in the Veda hi is optionally pit; so the optional pit-ness is established; if it is not pit, sārvadhātukam apit makes it ṅit and kṅiti ca would prohibit guṇa — it does not prohibit here; the final letter [dh] of the root is lost by Vedic usage. - gṛṇate: root gṝ śabde; laṭ → śatṛ; śnā; pvādīnāṃ hrasvaḥ: shortening; śnābhyastayor ātaḥ [Pā. 6-4-112 as read]: the loss of the ā; śatur anumo nadyajādī [Pā. 6-1-173 as read]: the ending ṅe [print: je] is acute. - yaviṣṭhya: "explained at [Ṛg. 1-36-6 as read [?]]." - praskaṇvasya: "pra means origin, from the sage Kaṇva, of whom [he is]; a bahuvrīhi; praskaṇvahariścandrāv ṛṣī — प्रस्कण्वहरिश्चन्द्रावृषी — [Pā. 6-1-153 as read]: the augment suṭ is irregularly given in praskaṇva and hariścandra when a ṛṣi is meant; the accent of the first member." - pratiran: the root tira with pra in the sense of increase. - namasya: namovarivaścitraṅaḥ kyac — नमोवरिवश्चित्रङः क्यच् — [Pā. 3-1-19 as read]: by the vārttika namasaḥ pūjāyām kyac after namas in the sense of honour; accent of the suffix; anyeṣām api dṛśyate: the long vowel in the Saṃhitā. - daivyam: devāda yañañau — देवाद्यञ्ञौ — [Pā. 4-1-85 as read]: yañ and añ after deva in the prāgdīvyatīya senses; tasyedam: yañ; taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ vṛddhi; yasyeti ca the loss of the a of daiva, daivya; am; pūrvarūpa. Rik 6 ends here (|| 6 ||).

original p. 516

Rik 7

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

होतारं विश्ववेदसं सं हि त्वा विश इन्धते । स आ वह पुरुहूत प्रचेतसोऽग्ने देवाँ इह द्रवत् ॥ ७ ॥

hotāraṃ viśvavedasaṃ saṃ hi tvā viśa indhate | sa ā vaha puruhūta pracetaso 'gne devām̐ iha dravat || 7 ||

Pada-pāṭha

होतारम् । विश्वऽवेदसम् । सम् । हि । त्वा । विशः । इन्धते । सः । आ । वह । पुरुऽहूत । प्रऽचेतः । अग्ने । देवान् । इह । द्रवत् ॥ ७ ॥

hotāram | viśva-vedasam | sam | hi | tvā | viśaḥ | indhate | saḥ | ā | vaha | puru-hūta | pra-cetaḥ | agne | devān | iha | dravat || 7 || The Saṃhitā prints pracetaso 'gne; the Pada divides pra-cetaḥ | agne.

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya it breaks off at the foot of the page and continues on p. 517, not yet written

होतारं होमनिष्पादकं विश्ववेदसं सर्वज्ञं त्वामग्निं विशः प्रजाः समिन्धते हि । सम्यग्दीपयन्ति खलु । हे पुरुहूत बहुभिराहूताग्ने स त्वं प्रचेतसः प्रकृष्टज्ञानयुक्तान्देवानिह कर्मणि द्रवत् क्षिप्रमा वह । अभिमुख्येन प्रापय । द्रवदिति क्षिप्रनाम । द्रवदोषमिति तन्नामसु पाठात् ॥ विश्ववेदसं । विश्वानि वेत्तीति विश्ववेदाः । असुन् । मरुद्वृधादित्वात्पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वं ।…

hotāraṃ homaniṣpādakaṃ viśvavedasaṃ sarvajñaṃ tvām agniṃ viśaḥ prajāḥ samindhate hi | samyag dīpayanti khalu | he puruhūta bahubhir āhūtāgne sa tvaṃ pracetasaḥ prakṛṣṭajñānayuktān devān iha karmaṇi dravat kṣipram ā vaha | abhimukhyena prāpaya | dravad iti kṣipranāma | dravadoṣam iti tannāmasu pāṭhāt || viśvavedasaṃ | viśvāni vettīti viśvavedāḥ | asun | marudvṛdhāditvāt pūrvapadāntodāttatvaṃ |…

Translation of this part: "Hotāram, the accomplisher of the offering; viśvavedasam, all-knowing — you, Agni, the viśaḥ, the people, sam indhate hi, indeed kindle well. O puruhūta, [you] called by many, Agni, such as you are, pracetasaḥ, the gods endowed with excellent knowledge, iha, here in the rite, dravat, quickly, ā vaha, bring, make [them] reach [us] face to face. 'Dravat' is a name for 'quick', since it is read among its names ('dravadoṣam' and so on [?]). Viśvavedasam: 'viśvāni vetti'; asun; because it is of the marudvṛdhādi [group], the first member is final-acute…" the sentence continues on p. 517.

Rik 44.7, continued from p. 517; the Saṃhitā, Pada and the beginning of the bhāṣya are above

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya, end

… यद्वा । वेद इति धननाम । विश्वानि वेदांसि यस्यासौ विश्ववेदा । बहुव्रीहौ विश्वं संज्ञायामिति पूर्वपदान्तोदात्तत्वं । इन्धते । ञिइन्धी दीप्तौ । श्नसोरल्लोप इत्यकारलोपः । श्नान्नलोपः । पा. ६-४-२३ [?] । प्रत्ययस्वरः । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः ॥ ७ ॥

… yadvā | veda iti dhananāma | viśvāni vedāṃsi yasyāsau viśvavedā | bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām iti pūrvapadāntodāttatvaṃ | indhate | ñi indhī dīptau | śnasor allopa ity akāralopaḥ | śnān nalopaḥ | pā. 6-4-23 [?] | pratyayasvaraḥ | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ || 7 ||

Translation of the end: "… Or: veda is a name for wealth; 'viśvāni vedāṃsi yasya', he who has all wealth: viśvavedāḥ; in the bahuvrīhi the first member is final-acute by viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām. Indhate: root ñi indhī dīptau; the loss of a by śnasor allopaḥ; the loss of n by śnān nalopaḥ [Pā. 6-4-23 [?]]; accent of the suffix; the prohibition of nighāta by hi ca."

Pratipadārtha — "hotāram — [you who are] the accomplisher of the offering; viśvavedasam — and all-knowing; tvā — you; viśaḥ — all the people; sam indhate hi — it is right [to say that] they make [you] blaze well; puruhūta — O [you who are] called by many; agne — O Agni; saḥ — that you; pracetasaḥ — endowed with excellent knowledge; devān — the gods; iha — to this sacrificial rite; dravat — with promptness; ā vaha — bring [them] face to face."

Bhāvārtha — "O Agni, since you are all-knowing and the accomplisher of the offering, all the people make you blaze well in the sacrifice. They all give you invitations. Accept their invitations and bring promptly to this rite of ours the gods endowed with excellent knowledge."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 517) — "O Agni, the people kindle you, the all-knowing invoker ( Agani [sic] ) invoked [printed "nvoked"] by many, you bring hither, the wise gods quickly."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 517 - viśaḥ — "prajāḥ, people, that is, priests and others who praise you in the sacrifice." - pracetasaḥ = prakṛṣṭajñānayuktān — "gods of excellent knowledge." - dravat — "quickly. Since the word dravat is read among the twenty-six names of 'quick' beginning with nu, makṣu, dravat means promptly, quickly."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 517–518 — grammar pages, noted briefly - hotāram: root hu dānādanayoḥ; tṛc; guṇa, upadhādīrgha; am. - viśvavedasam: "viśvāni vetti": root vida jñāne; sarvadhātubhyo 'sun [Uṇ. 4-[?] as read]; marudvṛdhādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṃkhyānam gives the first member final-acute; or veda = wealth: "he whose wealth is all": a bahuvrīhi; bahuvrīhau viśvaṃ saṃjñāyām [Pā. 6-2-106 as read]: when a name is meant, the word viśva as the first member of a bahuvrīhi is final-acute. - indhate: root ñi indhī dīptau, rudhādi, ātmanepada; laṭ, jha; ātmanepadeṣv nataḥ: at for jha; rudhādibhyaḥ śnam; śnasor allopaḥ [Pā. 6-4-111 as read]: the a of śna is lost before a kit or ṅit sārvadhātuka; śnān nalopaḥ [Pā. 6-4-23 as read]: the n of the root, after śna, is lost; ṭi → e by ṭita ātmanepadānāṃ ṭer e; ād ādyudāttaś ca [as read]: since the substitute at is counted as in the upadeśa (āyannādiṣūpadeśivadvacanaṃ svarasiddhyartham), the at is first-syllable acute and by ādyudāttaś ca the suffix ate is acute; hi ca prohibits the wholly-unaccented. Rik 7 ends here (|| 7 ||).

original pp. 518–521

Rik 8

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

सवितारमुषसमश्विना भगमग्निं व्युष्टिषु क्षपः । कण्वासस्त्वा सुतसोमास इन्धते हव्यवाहं स्वध्वर ॥ ८ ॥

savitāram uṣasam aśvinā bhagam agniṃ vyuṣṭiṣu kṣapaḥ | kaṇvāsas tvā sutasomāsa indhate havyavāhaṃ svadhvara || 8 ||

Pada-pāṭha

सवितारम् । उषसम् । अश्विना । भगम् । अग्निम् । विऽउष्टिषु । क्षपः । कण्वासः । त्वा । सुतऽसोमासः । इन्धते । हव्यऽवाहम् । सुऽअध्वर ॥ ८ ॥

savitāram | uṣasam | aśvinā | bhagam | agnim | vi-uṣṭiṣu | kṣapaḥ | kaṇvāsaḥ | tvā | suta-somāsaḥ | indhate | havya-vāham | su-adhvara || 8 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे स्वध्वर शोभनयोगयुक्ताग्ने । व्युष्टिषूषःकालेषु श्रवोऽन्नमाहुतिरूपमभिलक्ष्य सवित्रादीन्देवानावहेत्यनुवर्तते । स्वध्वरेत्याहवनीयोग्नेः सम्बोधनं । अग्निमिति हविष उद्देश्यं देवतान्तरमुच्यते सुतसोमासोऽभिषुतसोमाः कण्वासो मेधाविन ऋत्विजो हव्यवाहं हविषः प्रापकमाहवनीयं त्वामिन्धते दीपयन्ति ॥ व्युष्टिषु । उभी विवासे । विवासो वर्जनं । व्युच्छ्यते तमसा वर्ज्यते इति व्युष्टिरुषःकालः । कर्मणि क्तिनि क्रादौ च नितीति गतेः प्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । संहितायामुदात्तस्वरितयोर्यण इति परस्यानुदात्तस्य स्वरितत्वं । क्षपः । क्षपेति रात्रिनाम । जस्यातो धातोः । पा. ६-४-१४० । इत्यत्रात इति योगविभागादाकारलोपः । सुतसोमासः । सुतः सोमो यैस्ते । निष्ठेति पूर्वनिपातः । पा. २-२-३६ । बहुव्रीहौ पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । हव्यवाहं । हव्यं वहतीति हव्यवाट् । वहश्चेति ण्विप्रत्ययः ॥ ८ ॥

he svadhvara śobhanayogayuktāgne | vyuṣṭiṣūṣaḥkāleṣu śravo 'nnam āhutirūpam abhilakṣya savitrādīn devān āvahety anuvartate | svadhvarety āhavanīyognaḥ saṃbodhanaṃ | agnim iti haviṣa uddeśyaṃ devatāntaram ucyate sutasomāso 'bhiṣutasomāḥ kaṇvāso medhāvina ṛtvijo havyavāhaṃ haviṣaḥ prāpakam āhavanīyaṃ tvām indhate dīpayanti || vyuṣṭiṣu | ubhī vivāse | vivāso varjanaṃ | vyucchyate tamasā varjyate iti vyuṣṭir uṣaḥkālaḥ | karmaṇi ktini krādau ca niti iti gateḥ prakṛtisvaratvaṃ | saṃhitāyām udāttasvaritayor yaṇa iti parasyānudāttasya svaritatvaṃ | kṣapaḥ | kṣapeti rātrināma | jasy āto dhātoḥ | pā. 6-4-140 | ity atrāta iti yogavibhāgād ākāralopaḥ | sutasomāsaḥ | sutaḥ somo yais te | niṣṭheti pūrvanipātaḥ | pā. 2-2-36 | bahuvrīhau pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | havyavāhaṃ | havyaṃ vahatīti havyavāṭ | vahaś ceti ṇvipratyayaḥ || 8 || In the bhāṣya "āhavanīyognaḥ" (for āhavanīyo 'gneḥ) is as read, doubtful [?]; the clause "ktini krādau ca niti" and the Pāṇini numbers are read with doubt.

Translation: "O svadhvara, Agni, endowed with fine sacrificial connections — vyuṣṭiṣu, at the times of dawn, śravaḥ, food, in the form of the offering, aiming at: 'bring the gods beginning with Savitṛ' is carried over. 'Svadhvara' is the address to the Āhavanīya fire. 'Agnim' is said of another deity who is the object of the oblation. Sutasomāsaḥ, those who have pressed the Soma, kaṇvāsaḥ, the wise priests, havyavāham, the bearer of oblations, the Āhavanīya which conveys the oblation — you — indhate, they kindle. Vyuṣṭiṣu: root ubhī vivāse; 'vivāsaḥ' is varjanam; the time of dawn, when [the world] is specially dispelled by darkness. Kṣapaḥ: kṣapā is a name for night; the loss of the ā by the yogavibhāga of ata in jasy āto dhātoḥ [Pā. 6-4-140]. Sutasomāsaḥ: '[those] by whom the Soma is pressed'; niṣṭhā comes first in the compound [Pā. 2-2-36]; the accent of the first member in the bahuvrīhi. Havyavāham: 'havyaṃ vahati', havyavāṭ; ṇvip by vahaś ca."

Pratipadārtha — "svadhvara — O Agni, endowed with excellent sacrifices; kṣapaḥ — after the night; vyuṣṭiṣu — at the times of dawn; savitāram — Savitṛ; uṣasam — Uṣas; aśvinā — the Aśvin deities; bhagam — Bhaga; agnim — [and] the god Agni (bring [them]); sutasomāsaḥ — those who have the Soma juice [pressed]; kaṇvāsaḥ — the wise priests; havyavāham — you who carry the oblations; indhate — they make [you] blaze."

Bhāvārtha — "O Agni, you are endowed with excellent sacrifices. At the times of dawn, immediately after the night, bring to our sacrifice Savitṛ, Uṣas, the Aśvin deities, Bhaga and the god Agni. The wise priests press the Soma juice and make you, who carry the oblations, blaze."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 519) — "O Agni, who is worshipped well in the sacrifices, bring hither, at the break of the day preceeding [sic] the night, Savitru, Ushas, the Aswins, Bhaga and Agni ; the Kanwas having pressed and poured out the soma libations, kindle you, the carrier of oblation ( to the gods )." The source's heading for this English reads "Englih Translation" — a misprint [sic]; "Agni" is printed "Agui" once.

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 520 - savitāram, uṣasam, aśvinā, bhagam, agnim — "the ṛṣi prays Agni to come bringing these deities. Since Agni is also among the deities here, it is impossible that Agni should call Agni himself. So the main intention is: 'together with these deities we invite you too'." - kṣapaḥ — "kṣapā means night; here 'after the night'; since the word kṣapā is read among the twenty-three names of night beginning with śyāvī, kṣapā, the word means night." - kaṇvāsaḥ — "the sons of the ṛṣi Kaṇva, or the descendants of the ṛṣi Kaṇva." - sutasomāsaḥ — "sutaḥ somo yaiḥ te: those who have pressed and made ready the Soma juice." - indhate — "they kindle; they make blaze; after churning the fire, they first establish that fire in the fire-pit called Āhavanīya, set up in the eastern part of the sacrificial altar." - svadhvara = śobhanayogayuktāgne — "one who is worshipped in excellent sacrifices."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 520–521 — grammar pages, noted briefly - vyuṣṭiṣu: "explained in the third mantra of this sūkta." - kṣapaḥ: "kṣapā is a name for night. After it jas; jasy āto dhātoḥ [Pā. 6-4-140 as read]: the final ā of a bha-named aṅga that ends in an ā-ending root is lost; but kṣapā is not an ā-ending root; so this sūtra cannot give the loss here. Here the sūtra has been divided (yogavibhāga) into ātaḥ: [it provides that] the final ā of an ā-ending aṅga that has the bha name is lost; the sense of the second part is as said before; here the loss of the ā comes by ātaḥ." - sutasomāsaḥ: root ṣuñ abhiṣave; kta in the passive sense; "sutaḥ somo yaiḥ te", a bahuvrīhi; niṣṭhā [Pā. 2-2-36 as read]: in a bahuvrīhi a kta/ktavatu-ending word is used as the first member; so suta is put first; bahuvrīhau prakṛtyā pūrvapadam gives the accent of the first member. - havyavāham: the same ṇyuṭ as in the first pāda of Rik 2 [Ṛg. 1-44-2] is possible by havye 'nantaḥpādam; but here the word stands at the beginning of the fourth pāda, so havye 'nantaḥ… does not apply; and vahaś ca — वहश्च — [Pā. 3-2-64 as read]: when a subanta is the upapada, ṇvi after vah; so ṇvi; upadhāvṛddhi, ṭh-tva [ḍhatva] and the like. Rik 8 ends here (|| 8 ||).

original pp. 521–524

Rik 9

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

पतिर्ह्यध्वराणामग्ने दूतो विशामसि । उषर्बुध आ वह सोमपीतये देवाँ अद्य स्वर्दृशः ॥ ९ ॥

patir hy adhvarāṇām agne dūto viśām asi | uṣarbudha ā vaha somapītaye devām̐ adya svardṛśaḥ || 9 ||

Pada-pāṭha

पतिः । हि । अध्वराणाम् । अग्ने । दूतः । विशाम् । असि । उषःऽबुधः । आ । वह । सोमऽपीतये । देवान् । अद्य । स्वःऽदृशः ॥ ९ ॥

patiḥ | hi | adhvarāṇām | agne | dūtaḥ | viśām | asi | uṣaḥ-budhaḥ | ā | vaha | soma-pītaye | devān | adya | svaḥ-dṛśaḥ || 9 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे अग्ने विशां प्रजानां सम्बन्धिनो येऽध्वरा योगास्तेषां पतिः पालकस्त्वं दूतोऽसि हि । देवानां वार्ताहारो भवसि खलु । उषर्बुध उषःकाले प्रबुद्धान् स्वर्दृशः सूर्यदर्शिनो देवानद्यास्मिन्दिने सोमपीतये सोमपानार्थमा वह । अभिमुख्येन प्रापय ॥ असि । हि चेति निघातप्रतिषेधः । सोमपीतये । पा पाने । स्थागापापचो भाव इति भावे क्तिन् । घुमास्थेतीत्वं । सोमस्य पीतिः । दासीभारादित्वात्पूर्वपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं । स्वर्दृशः । सुष्ठ्वर्ति गच्छतीति स्वरादित्यः । अर्तेरन्येभ्योऽपि दृश्यन्त इति विच् । तं पश्यन्तीति स्वर्दृशः । क्विप्चेति क्विप् । कृदुत्तरपदप्रकृतिस्वरत्वं ॥ ९ ॥

he agne viśāṃ prajānāṃ sambandhino ye 'dhvarā yogās teṣāṃ patiḥ pālakas tvaṃ dūto 'si hi | devānāṃ vārtāhāro bhavasi khalu | uṣarbudha uṣaḥkāle prabuddhān svardṛśaḥ sūryadarśino devān adyāsmin dine somapītaye somapānārtham ā vaha | abhimukhyena prāpaya || asi | hi ceti nighātapratiṣedhaḥ | somapītaye | pā pāne | sthāgāpāpaco bhāva iti bhāve ktin | ghumāstheti ītvaṃ | somasya pītiḥ | dāsībhārāditvāt pūrvapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ | svardṛśaḥ | suṣṭhv arti gacchatīti svarādityaḥ | arter anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyanta iti vic | taṃ paśyantīti svardṛśaḥ | kvip ceti kvip | kṛduttarapadaprakṛtisvaratvaṃ || 9 || In the grammatical tail the words "svarādityaḥ" (for svar ādityaḥ, 'svar' = the Sun) and the rule-name sthāgāpāpaco bhāve are as read, doubtful [?].

Translation: "O Agni, you, the patiḥ, the protector, of the adhvarāṇām, sacrifices that belong to viśām, the people — dūtaḥ asi hi, you are the messenger of the gods, the carrier of tidings. Uṣarbudhaḥ, the gods who have awakened at the time of Uṣas, svardṛśaḥ, who see the sun, adya, today, somapītaye, for the drinking of Soma, ā vaha, bring, make [them] reach face to face. Asi: the prohibition of nighāta by hi ca. Somapītaye: root pā pāne; ktin in the abstract sense by sthāgāpāpacaḥ [as read]; ī by ghumāsthā…; 'the drinking of Soma': by belonging to the dāsībhārādi group the first member keeps its accent. Svardṛśaḥ: 'suṣṭhu arti gacchati' [gives] svar, the sun; vic by anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante after ṛ; 'taṃ paśyanti', those who see him: svardṛśaḥ; kvip by kvip ca; the accent of the first member in a compound ending in a kṛt."

Pratipadārtha — "agne — O Agni; viśām — of the people; adhvarāṇām — of the sacrifices; patiḥ — as protector; dūtaḥ — as messenger of the gods; asi hi — you are; uṣarbudhaḥ — those who rise at dawn; svardṛśaḥ — and who look at the sun; devān — the gods; adya — today; somapītaye — for the drinking of the Soma juice; ā vaha — bring [them] face to face to [us]."

Bhāvārtha — "O Agni, you are the protector of the sacrifices of the people and the messenger of the gods. Therefore you are a benefactor equally to the gods and to men. The gods awake at dawn and look at the sun. Bring those gods to our sacrificial place to drink the Soma juice."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 522) — "O Agni, you are the protector of the sacrifices of the people and the messenger of the gods ; bring hither to-day the gods awaking at dawn and seeing the sun, to drink the Soma-juice."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), pp. 522–523 - adhvarāṇāṃ patiḥ — "yajñānāṃ pālakaḥ: the protector of sacrifices: 'protector of sacrifices or lord of the sacrifices' (English as printed). Lord of sacrifices: since Agni has pre-eminence in sacrifices, he is called yajñapati." - viśāṃ — "prajānāṃ sambandhino ye adhvarās teṣām: the commentator says it means 'the protector of the sacrifices that the people perform'. Rather than this, it seems more suitable to connect the word viśām with the word dūtaḥ and take dūto viśām asi as 'you are the messenger who goes from the people to the gods'." - uṣarbudhaḥ — "the explanation of this word I have given in the first ṛk of this sūkta." - svardṛśaḥ — "suṣṭhu arti gacchatīti svaḥ — it is one who goes in the atmosphere; thus svaḥ means the Sun; those who see him are svardṛśaḥ. The gods are in heaven, so they look at the Sun who is in heaven. Or, taken with the word uṣarbudhaḥ: the gods who, rising at dawn, look at the Sun at the time of his rising."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 523–524 — grammar pages, noted briefly - patiḥ: root pā rakṣaṇe; pāter ḍatiḥ — पातेर्डतिः — [Uṇ. 4-[?] as read]: the suffix ḍati, with loss of ṭi; by the suffix accent first-syllable acute (as printed: ādyudātta). - adhvarāṇām: "na vidyate dhvaraḥ (injury) yeṣu te adhvarāḥ, of those"; a bahuvrīhi; nañ-subhyām gives the latter member final-acute. - agne: begins a pāda; the eighth-adhyāya unaccentedness does not come; āmantritasya ca gives first-syllable acute. - asi: root as bhuvi, adādi; sip; śap → luk; tāsasty… gives the loss of the s of the root; the prohibition of the wholly-unaccented by hi ca; sip being pit is unaccented. - somapītaye: "ṣuñ abhiṣave; mun… [Uṇ. 1-1-62 as read: ārtistusuhusṛghṛkṣiptabhāyāvāpadiyakṣinībhyo man]: the suffix man after ṣuñ, guṇa: soma; root pā pāne; sthāgāpāpacō bhāve — स्थागापापचो भावे — [Pā. 3-3-95 as read]: after these roots ktin in the abstract; ghumāsthāgāpājahātisāṃ hali [Pā. 6-4-66 as read]: ī for the ā of these roots before a kit or ñit ārdhadhātuka beginning with a consonant: pīti; 'somasya pītiḥ': a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; kurugārhapatarikta-guru-sūtajaratśleṣmīla [— the rule kurugārhapatarikta… is Pā. 6-2-42 as read]: a list of seven compounds — words belonging to the dāsībhārādi group keep the accent of the first member, so the first member keeps its accent; the first member is first-syllable acute by the nit-accent; so this stays. - svardṛśaḥ: "suṣṭhu ati = goes [well], hence svaḥ, the Sun; 'ṛ gatau' after su as upapada; anyebhyo 'pi dṛśyante [Pā. 3-2-75 as read]: manin, kvanip, vanip, vic — the four suffixes come after roots, hence vic; sārvadhātukārdhadhātukayoḥ gives guṇa with raparatva: su + ar; yaṇ: svar; 'svaḥ paśyanti'; kvip ca: after dṛśir prekṣaṇe, kvip, svardṛk; by gatikārakopapadāt kṛt the kṛt-ending latter member keeps its accent; accusative plural śas: svardṛśaḥ." Rik 9 ends here (|| 9 ||).

original p. 524

Rik 10

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

अग्ने पूर्वा अनूषसो विभावसो दीदेथ विश्वदर्शतः । असि ग्रामेष्वविता पुरोहितोऽसि यज्ञेषु मानुषः ॥ १० ॥

agne pūrvā anūṣaso vibhāvaso dīdetha viśvadarśataḥ | asi grāmeṣv avitā purohito 'si yajñeṣu mānuṣaḥ || 10 ||

Pada-pāṭha

अग्ने । पूर्वाः । अनु । उषसः । विभावसो इति विऽभावसो । दीदेथ । विश्वऽदर्शतः । असि । ग्रामेषु । अविता । पुरःऽहितः । असि । यज्ञेषु । मानुषः ॥ १० ॥

agne | pūrvāḥ | anu | uṣasaḥ | vibhāvaso iti vi-bhāvaso | dīdetha | viśva-darśataḥ | asi | grāmeṣu | avitā | puraḥ-hitaḥ | asi | yajñeṣu | mānuṣaḥ || 10 || The Saṃhitā prints anūṣasaḥ with a long ū where the Pada has anu uṣasaḥ; Both are given as printed. The bhāṣya of Rik 10 begins on p. 525, not yet written.

Rik 44.10, continued from p. 525

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे विभावसो विशिष्टप्रकाशनरूपधनवन्नग्ने विश्वदर्शतः सर्वैर्दर्शनीयस्त्वं । पूर्वा उषसोऽनु अतीतानुषःकालाननुलक्ष्य दीदेथ दीप्तवानसि । तादृशस्त्वं ग्रामेषु जननिवासस्थानेष्वविताऽसि । रक्षकोऽभवसि । यज्ञेष्वनुष्ठेयकर्मसु पुरोहितो वेदेः पूर्वस्यां दिश्यवस्थितो मानुषोऽसि । ऋत्विग्यजमानानां मनुष्याणां हितोऽसि ॥

he vibhāvaso viśiṣṭaprakāśanarūpadhanavann agne viśvadarśataḥ sarvair darśanīyas tvaṃ | pūrvā uṣaso 'nu atītān uṣaḥkālān anulakṣya dīdetha dīptavān asi | tādṛśas tvaṃ grāmeṣu jananivāsasthāneṣv avitā 'si | rakṣako 'bhavasi | yajñeṣv anuṣṭheyakarmasu purohito vedeḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśy avasthito mānuṣo 'si | ṛtvigyajamānānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ hito 'si ||

Translation: "O Agni, vibhāvaso, you whose wealth is the splendour of special brilliance; viśvadarśataḥ, to be seen by all: you have shone, pūrvā uṣasaḥ anu, following (keeping in view) the past times of dawn — you have been blazing. Such as you are, you are the protector, avitā, in grāmeṣu, the dwelling-places of people; you are the guardian. In yajñeṣu, in the rites to be performed, you are purohitaḥ, set in front, placed on the east side of the altar; you are mānuṣaḥ, beneficial to the human beings, the priests and the sacrificers."

Grammatical tail characterized; the numerals are as read, doubtful [?] - dīdetha: the root dīdī is of the Veda only; the iṭ augment is not added because the grammarians' augment-rules are not invariable (āgamaśāstram anityam, as printed); doubling is avoided by the statement "in the doubling-section, optionally in the Chandas" (cited from the Kāśikā, number as read "6-1-8-1" [?]). - viśvadarśataḥ: "to be seen by all"; the suffix atac after dṛś by a rule beginning bhṛmṛdṛśi… (as printed); the first member keeps its end-acute, the word being of the marudvṛdh-class (Pā. 6-2-106 as read [?]). - purohitaḥ: puras formed with the suffix asi after pūrva, adhara, avara (the rule beginning pūrvādharāvarāṇām asi puradhavaś caiṣām, as printed); the word is indeclinable because a taddhita that does not take all case-endings is avyaya (Pā. 1-1-38 would be the standard number; as printed it is hard to read [?]); then gati-designation (Pā. 1-4-62 as read) and the gati-compound, with the first member retaining its own accent by gatir anantaraḥ. - Closing numeral of the Rik: "|| 10 ||".

Pratipadārtha — "vibhāvaso — O Agni, who have the wealth of illuminating all; agne — O Agni; viśvadarśataḥ — you who are to be seen by the eyes of all; pūrvāḥ uṣasaḥ anu — after the many dawns that have passed; dīdetha — you have made bright (such as you); grāmeṣu — in the villages (where people live); avitā — as protector; asi — you are; yajñeṣu — in the sacrificial rites; purohitaḥ — seated in the eastern part of the altar; mānuṣaḥ — as one beneficial to men (priests and sacrificers); asi — you are."

Bhāvārtha — "O Agni, by the greatness of your brilliance you not only illuminate everything in the world but are visible to all people. You have lit up thousands of dawns that have passed. Such a great one, you are the protector of every village where men dwell. Such a protector, you are purohita in our sacrifices, that is, seated in the eastern part of the altar, and are the benefactor of men, both priests and sacrificers."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 526) — "Resplendent Agni, visible to all, you have always shone after many preceding dawns [sic: "dawn⁠s" with a raised s], you are the protector of people in villages [sic: "iu"], and you are placed in front (on the east side of ths [sic] altar) for the benefit of man-" (the sentence breaks off at the end of the printed line; the last word is evidently "mankind", the rest of the word is not in the print as it appears).

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 526 - anu uṣasaḥ — "after the dawns, that is, every day after the dawn-times, before the sun's rising." - vibhāvaso — "viśiṣṭaprakāśarūpadhanavān: one who has the capacity to illuminate special things; one whose wealth is that capacity, i.e. who shines well, who blazes brightly." - dīdetha — "dīdeśiś chandaso dīptikarmā [reading doubtful, ?]: you shine; you are shining." - viśvadarśataḥ — "sarvair darśanīyaḥ: one who is looked at by all; you whom all see." - purohitaḥ — "vedeḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśy avasthitaḥ: established in the form of the āhavanīya on the east of the altar; one who is in front of the sacrifice. The explanation of this word is given in the Special Topics of the first ṛk of the first sūkta of the first maṇḍala, Ṛgveda Saṃhitā part 1, pp. 614–615 [numerals as read, ?]; see there." - mānuṣaḥ — "ṛtvigyajamānānāṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ hito 'si: the commentator has explained the word mānuṣaḥ as one who does good to people such as priests and sacrificers. But, taking the words purohito 'si yajñeṣu mānuṣaḥ together as general ('of men'), 'in the sacrifices that men perform you are purohita'; purohita means one placed in the foremost position, or one established in the āhavanīya fire-pit on the east side of the altar. If this sense is given, the meaning fits properly."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 526–527 — grammar pages, noted briefly - dīdetha: root dīdī dīptau, used in the Veda only; liṭ, sip, thal in place of sip by a rule beginning parasmaipadānāṃ ṇalatusus… (as printed); doubling avoided by the Kāśikā statement quoted in the bhāṣya, hence liṭ-doubling absent; the iṭ augment likewise does not come (āgamaśāstram anityam, as printed); guṇa: dīdetha; the all-unaccented (sarvānudātta) does not come since the word is at the beginning of a pāda; the end-acute from the root remains. - viśvadarśataḥ: root viś praveśane; the suffix kvan by an Uṇādi-sūtra beginning āśū pṛṣi… (as printed, number not legible [?]); the word is ādyudātta by nit (the suffix being nit). For dṛś prekṣaṇe: the suffix atac by "bhṛmṛdṛśi yajiparvi pacy amitanināmi haryibhyo 'tac" (Uṇ. 3-[?]0 as read); dṛś + ata, guṇa; viśvaiḥ darśataḥ = "darśanīyaḥ, one fit to be seen by all". By the antodātta-rule: "marudvṛdhādīnāṃ chandasy upasaṅkhyānam" (Pā. 6-2-106 [vārttika, as read, ?]) the first member gets end-acute. - purohitaḥ: pūrvādharāvarāṇām asi puradhavaś caiṣām (Pā. 5-3-39 as read [?]): after pūrva, adhara, avara, the suffix asi (in the senses of direction, place or time), and in place of pūrva, pur; of adhara, adh; of avara, av. Here pūrva + asi → pur + as = puras. taddhitaś cāsarvavibhaktiḥ (Pā. 1-1-38 [?]): a taddhita-ending word that cannot take all the case-endings is called avyaya; so puras is an indeclinable. The taddhita-suffixes counted begin with bahvalpārthāc chas kārakād anyatarasyām (Pā. 5-4-42 [?]) and run to samāsāntāḥ (Pā. 5-4-68 [?]), so asi is counted. puro 'vyayam (Pā. 1-4-67 as read, [?]): gati-designation; kugatiprādayaḥ gives the compound with hita; gatir anantaraḥ (Pā. 6-2-49 as read [?]): when a word ending with a karmaṇi-suffix follows, the preceding gati retains its natural accent. The word puras has end-acute by its suffix. From ḍudhāñ, the kta suffix; dadhāter hiḥ (Pā. 7-4-42 as read [?]): hi in place of dhā; hita. || 10 || End of Rik 44.10 on printed p. 527.

original pp. 528–531

Rik 11

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

नि त्वा यज्ञस्य साधनमग्ने होतारमृत्विजम् । मनुष्वद्देव धीमहि प्रचेतसं जीरं दूतममर्त्यम् ॥ ११ ॥

ni tvā yajñasya sādhanam agne hotāram ṛtvijam | manuṣvad deva dhīmahi pracetasaṃ jīraṃ dūtam amartyam || 11 ||

Pada-pāṭha

नि । त्वा । यज्ञस्य । साधनम् । अग्ने । होतारम् । ऋत्विजम् । मनुष्वत् । देव । धीमहि । प्रऽचेतसम् । जीरम् । दूतम् । अमर्त्यम् ॥ ११ ॥

ni | tvā | yajñasya | sādhanam | agne | hotāram | ṛtvijam | manuṣvat | deva | dhīmahi | pra-cetasam | jīram | dūtam | amartyam || 11 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे अग्ने देव मनुष्वत् यथा मनुर्यागदेशे निदधाति तद्वद्वयमपि त्वां नि धीमहि । अत्र स्थापयामः । कीदृशं । यज्ञस्य साधनं यज्ञनिष्पादकं होतारमृत्विजं ऋतौ वसन्तादिके यष्टारं प्रचेतसं प्रकृष्टप्रज्ञानयुक्तं जीरं शत्रूणां वयोहानिकरं दूतं देवानां दूतस्थानीयं अमर्त्यं मरणरहितं ॥

he agne deva manuṣvat yathā manur yāgadeśe nidadhāti tadvad vayam api tvāṃ ni dhīmahi | atra sthāpayāmaḥ | kīdṛśaṃ | yajñasya sādhanaṃ yajñaniṣpādakaṃ hotāram ṛtvijaṃ ṛtau vasantādike yaṣṭāraṃ pracetasaṃ prakṛṣṭaprajñānayuktaṃ jīraṃ śatrūṇāṃ vayohānikaraṃ dūtaṃ devānāṃ dūtasthānīyaṃ amartyaṃ maraṇarahitaṃ ||

Translation: "O Agni, O god! Manuṣvat, as Manu places (you) at the place of the sacrifice, even so we also ni dhīmahi, set you down, establish you here. What kind of one? Yajñasya sādhanam, the accomplisher of the sacrifice; hotāram ṛtvijam, the sacrificer in the seasons such as the spring; pracetasam, endowed with excellent wisdom; jīram, the one who diminishes the life of enemies; dūtam, standing in the place of messenger of the gods; amartyam, free from death."

Grammatical tail p. 528 foot; characterized, the sūtra number as read [?] - manuṣvat: the word manas (manus) ends with the Uṇādi suffix asi; the suffix vati by the rule "tena tulyaṃ kriyā ced vatiḥ" (Pā. 5-1-115 as read [?]) — "vati in the sense of 'equal to that' if it is an action". Because the word is of the ayasmaya class (as printed, ayasmayādītvena), it takes the bha-designation, so the ru-change and so on do not arise. - dhīmahi: root dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; loss of the reduplicative syllable after liṅ is Vedic (lin-ābhyāsa-lopaś chāndasaḥ, as printed). - jīram: the root ju is a sautra root (taken from the sūtras, not from the root-list); the suffix rak by "jorī ca" (Uṇ. 2-[?] as read); Kātyāyana says "raki jyaḥ saṃprasāraṇe jīra iti" (as printed).

Pratipadārtha — "agne deva — O god Agni; yajñasya sādhanam — as the accomplisher of the sacrifice; hotāram ṛtvijam — as one who performs the sacrifice in the seasons beginning with spring; pracetasam — as one endowed with excellent knowledge; jīram — as the destroyer of the lives of enemies; dūtam — as the messenger of the gods; amartyam — as one who is free from death; tvā — you; manuṣvat — in the manner in which Manu established (you) in the sacrificial ground; (vayam — we also) nidhīmahi — establish (you) here."

Bhāvārtha — "O god Agni, you are the accomplisher of the sacrifice. You are one who sacrifices in the seasons beginning with spring, being endowed with excellent knowledge. You destroy the lives of enemies and are free from death. Since you are the messenger of the gods, the destroyer of enemies and the nourisher of friends, Manu established you in the sacrificial ground. Like him we too establish you in this sacrificial ground."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 529) — "O Agni, we place you as Manu placed you in sacrificial altar [sic] ; you are the main factor of the sacrifice, the invoker, the ministering priest, the wise, the destroyer of enemies, immortal and the messenger of gods."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 529 - yajñasya sādhanam — "since Agni is absolutely necessary for performing a sacrifice, he is said to be the chief instrument of the sacrifice." - hotāram, ṛtvijam — "hotāram means one who invokes the deities in the sacrifice, or the one principal priest who recites the mantras in the sacrifice for the invocation of the deities. In the sacrifice the hotṛ has a place of great prominence. Ṛtvijam means one of the priests who take part in the sacrifice. In every sacrifice there are four chief priests, hotṛ, adhvaryu, udgātṛ and brahmā; these four, and also their assistant groups, are by custom called ṛtvij. When ṛtvij is said, it can be any one of them. For the explanation of these words see Ṛgveda Saṃhitā part 1, p. 615 [numeral as read, ?]." - manuṣvat — "manuvat: as the Prajāpati Manu established and set Agni in the sacrifice that he performed, in that manner; this is the meaning." - jīram — "ju iti sautro dhātuḥ; śatrūṇāṃ vayohānikaram: the destroyer of the life-span of enemies, one who diminishes (their life), one who makes (it) decay."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 530–531 — grammar pages, noted briefly; the crowded stretches not reproduced - yajñasya: root yaja devapūjādau; the suffix naṅ by "yajayācayataviccha-pracchā rakṣo naṅ" (Pā. 3-3-90 as read [?]) — यजयाचयतविच्छप्रश्नरक्षो नङ् — [as printed, the sūtra's wording is partly legible; it is given only in the standard form and the number as read]; yaj + na; the next step by "stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ" (Pā. 8-4-40 as read) — स्तोः श्चुना श्चुः — concerning the change of the dental nasal after the palatal; the suffix-accent (pratyayasvara) then arises. (The Kannada explanation of this step is partly unclear [?].) - manuṣvat: root mana jñāne; the Uṇādi suffix usi; man + us = manus; the analysis manuṣā tulyam "equal to Manu"; the rule tena tulyaṃ kriyā cet vatiḥ (Pā. 5-1-115 as read [?]): after a word in the instrumental the suffix vati in the sense of "equal", but only if what is equal is an action — here manuṣā tulyaṃ dhīmahi gives the action. Because vati comes, the word gets the bha-designation by ayasmayādīni chandasi (Pā. 1-4-20 as read), so there is no pada-designation; therefore the ru-change which has pada-designation as its cause by "sa sajuṣo ruḥ" (Pā. 8-2-66) does not come; nor does the u by "haśi ca" (Pā. 6-1-114). - deva: root divu … by the pacādi-rule (the rule beginning nandigrahipacādibhyaḥ…, as printed) the suffix ac; the vocative is unaccented (āmantritasya). - dhīmahi: dudhāñ dhāraṇapoṣaṇayoḥ; liṅ, mahiṅ, liṅaḥ sīyuṭ; liṅaḥ salopo 'nantyasya (the s is lost); lopo vyor vali (the y is lost); śap with ślu; doubling after ślu; the Vedic loss of the reduplicative syllable; dhā + īmahi; "śnābhyastayor ātaḥ" (Pā. 6-4-112 as read [?]) — the ā of the root is dropped when a non-kit/ṅit personal ending follows the śnā-suffix or reduplicated verb; dh + īmahi = dhīmahi. - jīram: ju gatau vege ca; this root is not in the root-list but is established by what Pāṇini says in the rule beginning ju-caṅkramya… (Pā. 3-2-150 as read [?]); roots that are thus used in sūtras are called sautra. The Uṇādi sūtra jorī ca (Uṇ. 2-[?] as read): after ju the suffix rak, and ī for the final letter, giving jīra. Some read instead of jorī ca the sūtra jyāś ca (Uṇ. 2-[?] as read): rak after the root jyā vayohānau; jyā + ra, and grahijyā-vayi… (Pā. 6-1-16 as read) gives saṃprasāraṇa; saṃprasāraṇāc ca (Pā. 6-1-108) gives the earlier form (pūrvarūpa); halaḥ (Pā. 6-4-2) lengthens the final of the stem after a saṃprasāraṇa standing after a consonant: jīra. na dhātulopa ārdhadhātuke (Pā. 1-1-4) etc.; and Kātyāyana's vārttika "raki jyaḥ saṃprasāraṇam" is cited; hence the reading jyāśca is evidently the one approved by Kātyāyana. || 11 ||

original pp. 531–534

Rik 12

Saṃhitā-pāṭha

यद्देवानां मित्रमहः पुरोहितोऽन्तरो यासि दूत्यम् । सिन्धोरिव प्रस्वनितास ऊर्मयोऽग्नेर्भ्राजन्ते अर्चयः ॥ १२ ॥

yad devānāṃ mitramahaḥ purohito 'ntaro yāsi dūtyam | sindhor iva prasvanitāsa ūrmayo 'gner bhrājante arcayaḥ || 12 ||

Pada-pāṭha

यत् । देवानाम् । मित्रमहः इति मित्रऽमहः । पुरःऽहितः । अन्तरः । यासि । दूत्यम् । सिन्धोःऽइव । प्रऽस्वनितासः । ऊर्मयः । अग्नेः । भ्राजन्ते । अर्चयः ॥ १२ ॥

yat | devānām | mitramahaḥ iti mitra-mahaḥ | puraḥ-hitaḥ | antaraḥ | yāsi | dūtyam | sindhoḥ-iva | pra-svanitāsaḥ | ūrmayaḥ | agneḥ | bhrājante | arcayaḥ || 12 ||

Sāyaṇa-bhāṣya

हे मित्रमहो मित्राणां पूजकाग्ने यद्यदा पुरोहितस्त्वं वेदेः पूर्वस्यां दिशि स्थापितोऽन्तरो देवयजनमध्ये वर्तमानः सन् देवानां दूत्यं दूतकर्म यासि प्राप्नोषि तदानीमग्नेस्तवार्चयो दीप्तयो भ्राजन्ते । दीप्यन्ते । तत्र दृष्टान्तः । सिन्धोरिव यथा समुद्रस्य प्रस्वनितासः प्रकृष्टध्वनियुक्ता ऊर्मयस्तरंगा भ्राजन्ते तद्वत् ॥

he mitramaho mitrāṇāṃ pūjakāgne yad yadā purohitas tvaṃ vedeḥ pūrvasyāṃ diśi sthāpito 'ntaro devayajanamadhye vartamānaḥ san devānāṃ dūtyaṃ dūtakarma yāsi prāpnoṣi tadānīm agnes tavārcayo dīptayo bhrājante | dīpyante | tatra dṛṣṭāntaḥ | sindhor iva yathā samudrasya prasvanitāsaḥ prakṛṣṭadhvaniyuktā ūrmayas taraṅgā bhrājante tadvat ||

Translation: "O mitramahaḥ, O Agni, worshipped by friends (or: worshipper of friends); yat, when you, set up as purohita on the east side of the altar, being antaraḥ, in the middle of the place of divine worship, yāsi dūtyam, perform and attain the office of messenger of the gods, tadānīm, then your arcayaḥ, flames, bhrājante, blaze, shine. The simile: sindhor iva, just as the prasvanitāsaḥ, loudly resounding ūrmayaḥ, waves, of the ocean shine, so do they."

Grammatical tail characterized, numerals as read [?] - mitramahaḥ: root maha pūjāyām; "he who is honoured (mahyate) by friends, the priests"; the Uṇādi suffix asun. - yāsi: because of the yad-relation (yadvṛtta) the verb is not unaccented (anighāta). - dūtyam: "the work of a messenger"; the suffix yat by "dūtasya bhāgakarmaṇī" (Pā. 4-4-120 as read [?]); by the saying "all rules are optional in the Chandas" the initial acute does not arise, and by tit svaritam a svarita comes. - prasvanitāsaḥ: root svana / dhvana śabde; niṣṭhā in the abstract sense; "those whose sounding is excellent" (prakṛṣṭaṃ svanitaṃ yeṣāṃ te); the āsuk-augment (printed "āsugāgamaḥ", doubtful reading [?]; the grammar page names it asuk); in the bahuvrīhi the first member keeps its natural accent. - ūrmayaḥ: arter ūc ca (Uṇ. 4-[?] as read), the suffix mi.

Pratipadārtha — "mitramahaḥ — O Agni, worshipped by the priests or by friendly people; yat — when; purohitaḥ — placed as purohita in the eastern part of the altar; antaraḥ — being in the middle part of the sacrificial place; devānām — of the gods; dūtyam — the work of messenger; yāsi — you take up (then); agneḥ — of you, god Agni; arcayaḥ — the flames; sindhoḥ — of the ocean; prasvanitāsaḥ — roaring with sound; ūrmayaḥ — the waves; (iva — as if, shining); bhrājante — shine."

Bhāvārtha — "O god Agni, many priests worship you. When you are placed in the eastern part of the altar as purohita and, being in the middle of the sacrificial place, take up the work of messenger of the gods — then, since you alone carry all the oblations offered to all the gods, your flames rise very high. Then, like the waves of the ocean that roar and shine, they shine with sound and with brilliance."

English Translation (the source's own, p. 532) — "O Agni, you are being worshipped by the friendly priests ; when you are placed in front of the altar ( or as a Purohita at a sacrifice ) and are installed as the messenger of the gods, then your flames roar like the resounding billows of the ocean."

Special Topics (viśeṣa-viṣayagaḷu), p. 533 - yat — "yadā: when." - mitramahaḥ — "mitrair ṛtvigbhir mahyate pūjyate iti mitramahāḥ, tasya sambuddhir mitramahaḥ: one who is worshipped by the priests, who are friendly to you and objects of your affection." - purohitaḥ — "the explanation of this word was given at the tenth ṛk of this sūkta." - sindhor iva ūrmayaḥ — "like the waves of the ocean." - prasvanitāsaḥ — "svana dhvana śabde; prakṛṣṭaṃ svanitaṃ yeṣāṃ te prasvanitāḥ: making sound very loudly, roaring." - arcayaḥ — "the flames of Agni; the flames of Agni that blaze well, with a crackling, from the oblations such as ghee which the priests pour in the sacrifice. The idea is that they blaze up, as the waves of the ocean, struck by the wind, come to the shore and dash and roar loudly."

Vyākaraṇa-prakriyā pp. 533–534 — grammar pages, noted briefly - mitramahaḥ: analysis "mitraiḥ mahyate pūjyate"; root maha pūjāyām; the suffix asun by "sarvadhātubhyo 'sun" (Uṇ. 4-[?], as printed without a number that could be read). - yāsi: yadvṛttān nityam (Pā. 8-1-66 as read [?]) — यद्वृत्तान्नित्यम् — forbids the all-unaccented (sarvānudātta) of the verb. - dūtyam: dūtasya bhāgakarmaṇī (Pā. 4-4-120 as read [?]) — दूतस्य भागकर्मणी — the suffix yat in the senses of "share" and "work"; dūta + ya, yasyeti ca (the a is dropped); the rule on acute yato 'nāvaḥ is optional in the Veda by the maxim "sarve vidhayaś chandasi vikalpyante" (paribhāṣā, number as read "63" [?]), so does not come here; by tit svaritam a svarita arises.
